context:
Goal: main's push run skips by the proven-tree rule, so each merge does not cost a full run on main (CI speed).
Problem (rule): making `merge <pr> --ready` push a merge of main widens what the merge tool does to a PR branch, and the records commit that `--ready` also pushes is a one-parent commit that makes the review record stale. Only you can decide which record rule holds.
Based on (measured, coordinator 12:18 CST, relayed; triage read none of it): 0 of the last 8 main pushes skipped; #3402 head tree 2c29427dc8 against merge tree 28705afa96 (the coordinator read both). The lane read the code: `draft_step` in merge/merge.py never pushes a merge today, because `holds_base` (rule M3) lets a head lacking main's tip stand if the merge is clean; `live_review_state` ends its walk as stale at any one-parent commit, in either order of merge and records commit; the lane-lint walk (about merge.py line 1861) already skips a page-only commit "Rebuild the records page".
Based on (measured, from #3396's body, n=1): one full `checks` run after the records step took 44 min. The page changes in about 1 of 3 to 1 of 2 merges (triage's earlier walk, unchecked here).
Based on (measured, the lane's read-only Sonnet agent, relayed by the coordinator at 12:21 CST; neither the lane nor the coordinator re-read its rows): of the last 15 merges to main (08:09 to 18:13 UTC today), 9 had one or more other merges to main between the ready run's start and the PR's own merge (13 other merges across the 9; #3404 had 2), and 6 had none. So a merge of main at ready would leave head tree equal to merge tree for at most 6 of 15; the other 9 still mismatch. Ready-run length: median 39.4 min, range 29.7 to 79.0 (n=15; the 71.6 and 79.0 are #3279 and #3376). Unmeasured: the ready mark itself, pass or fail of each run, and merges not among the 15. The lane adds, unstudied: merging main right before the merge in the tool, or an owner pick on merge method (a squash gives no tree match either), would reach more than option a alone.
Based on (code, the lane's read of merge/merge.py on main at 245e168, relayed; the coordinator did not re-read it): today `draft_step` pushes one one-parent page commit (`commit_claim`, subject "Rebuild the records page", then `push_branch`) when `rebuild_records` changes the page; `ready_page_state` pushes nothing. Under 830 a, `--ready` pushes no page commit only if `--ready` stops rebuilding: a code change in `draft_step`, and the "stale page refused before any push" rule in the `--ready` docstring would go. Under 830 b it still pushes. Under 830 c the commit is still pushed, and whether the PR run skips for a page-only commit is unknown (no code read: `page_only` is used by the lane-lint walk, and main's push skip judges tree equality, not commit shape). So d's gain needs 830 a plus that code change.
Based on (ruling): push-skip-proven-tree (owner 12:18 CST Nov 13, item 729 a): skip the push re-run when the pushed tree equals the tree the PR tested. The standing grant (standing-merge-grant.md line 18) already lets the batch runner push a plain merge of main into a handed-in PR; the open part is only the record walk.
Related: owner item 830 (records page gone stale after a PR went ready). Its own options are a (merge as is, refresh the page in a draft PR after), b (keep the refusal) and c (skip CI on a records-only push). Which of them makes `--ready` push no records commit is the coordinator's reading, unchecked by triage.
Departs from: main — today `--ready` pushes no merge of main and one records commit; options a and b add a pushed merge of main at ready.
Meanwhile: the lane built nothing and waits. Nothing else waits on this item.
Update 15:06 CST Nov 14: you answered item 830 c (CI scope skips every job on a records-only push after a fully green head). So the ready records push stays, and option d reads as option b. Item 830 is closed.
No option is starred. The coordinator recommends d (with b as its fallback if 830 keeps the ready records push). The lane recommends c, the only option that widens nothing, and says a is the one that works if you put CI speed above the ruling. Options a, b and d each widen what the merge tool does or accepts, by the lane's count, so none is starred. The coordinator reads b and d as a change to one tool's own step that standing grant line 18 already allows by hand, and does not decide which reading holds. Your goal ranks CI speed first (23:49 CST Nov 13, the coordinator's citation, unchecked by triage), and c loses a full main run per merge (about 30 jobs).
Reply 16:34 CST Nov 14 (to your save "hasnt 830 been answered"): Yes. You answered item 830 on Nov 14 at 15:02 CST: option c, CI skips every job on a records-only push after a fully green head. That settled 830. It did not settle this item, which asks something else: may `merge --ready` push a merge of main so main's push run can skip. Your 830 answer makes option d (answer 830 first) moot: it now reads as b. No ruling of yours covers a, b or c, so this item stays open. Choices left: a, b, c.

options.gain: The push skip can fire, and the record survives the page commit. A merge of main at ready would leave the trees equal for at most 6 of the last 15 merges (the lane's count).
options.label: Merge main at ready, and the review record skips page-only commits (the lane's recommendation)
options.lose: One more PR run per ready that pushes nothing today; a wider record walk. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.gain: A smaller change and no widening of the record walk. A merge of main at ready would leave the trees equal for at most 6 of the last 15 merges (the lane's count).
options.label: Merge main at ready only; the record goes stale when the page changes
options.lose: A lane-printed fix check on about 1 of 3 to 1 of 2 PRs (the page changes that often by triage's earlier walk). A pushed merge of main at ready is a new merge-tool write, which the lane counts as widening the merge tool. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.lose: A full main run per merge, about 30 of 33-35 jobs (the last 8 main pushes). The lane recommends this: it is the only option that widens nothing.

options.gain: With 830 a: no records commit follows the pushed merge of main, the record stays, and the skip can fire (a clean merge of main keeps the record). This needs 830 a plus a code change in `draft_step` (the lane's read).
options.label: Answer item 830 first. Only 830 a (merge a ready green PR as is, refresh the page in a draft PR after) removes the ready records push; with 830 b or c, fall back to option b
options.lose: Waits on item 830. With 830 b or c the ready records push stays, a one-parent records commit follows the merge, and the record goes stale as in option b. The pushed merge of main it keeps is the same new merge-tool write as b, which the lane counts as widening the merge tool (the coordinator reads it as a change to one tool's own step that the standing grant already lets the runner do by hand). Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

short: May `merge --ready` push a merge of main so main's push run can skip?
title: To let main's push run skip, do you let `merge <pr> --ready` push a merge of main and make the review record skip page-only commits (a), push the merge only and accept a stale record when the page changes (b), leave it (c), or answer item 830 first (d)?
why: Main's push run skips only when the merged tree equals the tree the PR tested. Today 0 of the last 8 main pushes skipped. Making `--ready` push a merge of main widens what the merge tool does to a PR branch, and the records commit it also pushes makes the review record stale. You decide which record rule holds. The cause holds on degen too (runner 11's read, 12:20 CST, an Explore agent on Sonnet with REST job counts; relayed, unchecked by triage): in the last 8 main push runs of degen the skip fired 2 of 8, on exactly the 2 merges whose merge tree equalled the PR head tree; on the other 6 the trees differed and it did not fire. On home all 8 merges had equal trees but home has no push-skip job at all.
